big: A client asks, 'Which one gave more, this PMS or that AIF?' One quotes gross returns, the other net. Comparing them is unfair. Responsible selling starts with the client, not the numbers.

lines: Start with suitability: goal, horizon, liquidity, existing portfolio, risk capacity and experience. Share the Disclosure Document or PPM and explain fees, lock-ins, risks and exit terms in plain words. Never promise returns, never compare gross with net, and disclose conflicts such as commissions. Size it as a satellite and review every year.

q: What comes first when selling a PMS or AIF?
why: A brochure is not the basis.
A target is not the basis.

q: What should be shared with the client?
opts: Only a glossy flyer on top of it
Only a rumour from a friend
Nothing at all, to anyone, ever
why: It lists fees, risks and exits. This fits the facts given.
A flyer is not enough. It does not fit the facts given.
A rumour is not a document. It does not answer what was asked.
Sharing is required. It does not answer what was asked.

q: Why not compare gross and net figures?
opts: Net is always much lower here
Both are exactly the same thing
why: Net is lower only by the fees charged.
Gross figures are legal to quote.
The two differ by fees and costs.
Basis must match for a fair comparison.

opts: The RM's lunch menu today, any day
The make of the office lift here
why: A lift is not a conflict.

pts: Start with suitability, then share the document.
Never promise returns or mix gross and net.
Disclose conflicts; size small; review every year.
